title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Anthropic redeploys Claude Fable 5 globally (July 1) after US lifts export controls — its most capable, longest-autonomy model, now on Cowork + Claude Code
bullets.summary: Commerce lifted the June 12 export-control order; Fable 5 and Mythos 5 returned July 1 to the Claude Platform, Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Cowork with new cybersecurity-targeting classifiers, and can work autonomously longer than any prior Claude; Pro/Max/Team/select Enterprise get it for up to 50% of weekly limits through July 7, then via usage credits, with some routine coding falling back to Opus 4.8.
bullets.how: This is The Construct's own substrate: longer unattended autonomy is what the daily/weekly scans and Hermes background jobs need — route heavy-reasoning/long-run tasks to Fable 5, keep Opus 4.8 as the coding fallback, and mind credit burn after July 7.

bullets.title: MCP ships its biggest revision since launch — the 2026-07-28 spec release candidate: stateless core, Tasks, MCP Apps, OAuth-aligned auth
bullets.summary: The final spec lands July 28 with a stateless protocol core that scales on ordinary HTTP, an Extensions framework, a Tasks extension for long-running work, MCP Apps for server-rendered UIs, authorization aligned to OAuth/OpenID Connect, and a formal deprecation policy; the 10-week window is for SDK maintainers and Tier-1 SDKs to validate (9,400+ public servers, 80%+ of the Fortune 500 already on MCP).
bullets.how: The Construct runs its own MCP fleet: the Tasks extension formalizes our long-running scan/Hermes pattern, MCP Apps let our servers render UI back into Cowork, and the stateless core plus OAuth changes are plumbing to pilot before July 28, not after.

bullets.title: The new enterprise-ready MCP spec also widens the attack surface — security teams flag fresh risks in the RC
bullets.summary: As MCP hardens for enterprise (stateless HTTP, delegated OAuth, server-rendered Apps), analysts warn the same changes introduce new authorization, token-handling, and UI-injection risks that most current deployments aren't yet configured for.
bullets.how: Governance input for PRAGMA and The Construct: before adopting the new auth/Apps surface, treat each internal MCP server as a security-reviewed asset (scoped tokens, least-privilege, no blind UI rendering) — the skills-as-governed-assets posture extended to servers.

bullets.title: arXiv: 'Context Engineering: From Prompts to Corporate Multi-Agent Architecture'
bullets.summary: Frames context engineering as its own discipline (design and manage the whole informational environment an agent decides in) with five quality criteria — relevance, sufficiency, isolation, economy, provenance — plus intent engineering (encode org goals/values into infra) and specification engineering (a machine-readable corpus of corporate policy for autonomous multi-agent systems).
bullets.how: The theory under what we already do: CLAUDE.md as working memory, ~/.hermes/memories/ as the corpus, PRAXIS as provenance; score every agent's context against the five criteria and treat our locked rules as the specification-engineering layer.

praxis_lesson: July is a protocol-and-substrate inflection, not a shiny-model one — Fable 5 lifts the ceiling on unattended autonomy while the July 28 MCP spec rewrites how our own servers authenticate, run long tasks, and render UI. The Construct's move is to prep the plumbing now: pilot the MCP RC on one internal server, formalize scans/Hermes as MCP Tasks, and govern context and servers as security-reviewed assets — own the orchestration and governance layer while the model and protocol commoditize underneath us.
